contract_change_assessment.necessity: The literal old Pr(hat r≠r)→0 claim is false, not an imprecise proof of convergence in probability. Every estimator coordinate λ_i/n is rational. With r=(1/√2,1−1/√2), an allowed ordered full-rank qubit spectrum, equality is impossible at every n, so the probability of inequality is one. The successor retains this assertion to refute and explicitly asks for fixed-neighborhood concentration instead.

substantive_reconstruction.domain_and_counterexample: For n≥1 a partition has nonnegative decreasing row lengths summing to n; dividing by n gives a legitimate ordered probability vector, realized as a diagonal density matrix. n=0 has no λ/n estimator. The irrational example is decisive independently of the probability distribution. Even for rational spectra some sample counts cannot realize exact equality. Approximating the irrational example by (floor(nt),n−floor(nt))/n also shows D→0, so pointwise strict positivity off r supplies no uniform gap on the punctured simplex.
substantive_reconstruction.support_and_gap: Let h=d(d−1)/2 and fix ε>0. If p places mass on a zero component of r then D(p||r)=∞, and the given outcome bound forces its probability to zero. On the supported closed face, D=Σp_i log(p_i/r_i), with 0log0=0, is continuous; the closed ε-away set is compact and excludes its sole zero r, hence has minimum δ_ε>0 unless empty. With natural logarithms Pinsker additionally gives D≥||p−r||₁²/2, so δ_ε may be replaced by ε²/2.
substantive_reconstruction.count_and_limit: There are at most (n+1)^d possible padded row-length tuples. Summing the actual per-outcome estimate therefore gives Pr(||hat r−r||₁≥ε)≤(n+1)^(h+d)exp(−nδ_ε), and hence convergence to zero for fixed d. Keeping only exponent h would drop the union factor. The exponential dominates this polynomial, but not an n-dependent gap approaching zero. At d=1 or rank-one spectrum the only supported outcome has the matching one-row diagram. No constant lower mass for individual nearby atoms or exact matching conclusion is derived.
